title: What If...?
desc: Select a command to see a predicted outcome. No commands are actually executed.
emptyState: ← Select a command to see the prediction

jj-new.desc: Create a new empty working copy on top of the current WC.

jj-new-branch.desc: Branch from 2 commits back and create a new WC. Work in parallel without bookmarks.

jj-commit.desc: Finalize the current WC with a description and create a new empty WC. Equivalent to jj describe + jj new.

jj-squash.desc: Absorb WC changes into the parent commit (equivalent to git commit --amend).

jj-bookmark-set.desc: Set a bookmark (branch name) on the current WC.

jj-new-insert-before.desc: Insert a new commit before the current WC, between the WC and its parent.

jj-describe.desc: Change the description (commit message) of the current WC. DAG structure remains unchanged.

jj-edit-parent.desc: Move the WC to the parent commit. You can directly edit the parent.

jj-undo.desc: Undo the last operation and restore the repository to its previous state. A powerful feature with no direct git equivalent.

jj-restore.desc: Restore working copy files to the parent commit's state. Equivalent to git restore / git checkout --.

predict.jjNew: A new empty working copy is created, with the current WC becoming its parent. Your current changes remain as the parent commit.
predict.jjNewBranch: A new WC is created branching from 2 commits back. The original WC remains, so you can return via jj edit. No bookmark needed — tracked by change ID.
predict.jjNewBranch.gitEquiv: git stash && git checkout -b feature HEAD~2
predict.jjCommit: Similar to jj new, but also sets the commit message. The current WC gets a description and a new empty WC is created on top.
predict.jjSquash: WC changes are absorbed into the parent commit. The WC becomes empty but retains the same change ID.
predict.jjBookmarkSet: Bookmark 'main' is set on the current WC. Similar to 'git branch main', but jj bookmarks don't move automatically.
predict.jjNewInsertBefore: A new commit is inserted between the current WC and its parent. The new commit becomes the WC, and the original WC becomes its child.
predict.jjNewInsertBefore.gitEquiv: git rebase -i to insert a commit (multiple steps required)
predict.jjDescribe: The WC's commit message is changed. DAG structure remains the same. Neither change ID nor commit ID changes (since content is unchanged).
predict.jjUndo: The last operation is undone and the repository reverts to its previous state. The After view shows the actual previous operation state.
predict.jjUndo.fallback: The last operation is undone (showing same as Before because the previous state could not be retrieved).
predict.jjRestore: All files in the working copy are restored to the parent commit's state (WC becomes empty). Change ID is preserved and DAG structure remains the same. ⚠️ In colocate mode, git's staging area is also reset.
predict.jjEditParent: The working copy moves to the parent commit. You can directly edit the parent, and the original WC remains as a child. Use jj new to return when done.
predict.jjEditParent.gitEquiv: git stash && git checkout HEAD~ (detached HEAD)
